sentences: Locally checkable labeling problems have solutions whose validity can be inspected within neighborhoods of constant radius.
The source asks for a bounded-degree graph problem solvable in \(O(\log  n) \mathrm{LOCAL}\) rounds but requiring \(\Omega (n) \mathrm{CONGEST}\) rounds.
The two models differ only in message-size restrictions, so such a separation would isolate the cost of bandwidth.
The paper already separates them by a smaller gap on general graphs while showing matching complexities on trees.
A stronger example would demonstrate that even a locally verifiable task can require nearly global communication time when short messages replace unrestricted exchanges.
